rv.q: The Stakhanovite playwright, 44, is already back with another belter.
It is all so polished that the serrated edges of his life are lost, so accomplished that the mess of human conflict does not quite manage to fire its centre.
It is still pretty damn good: nobody brings the past to life with the verve of Graham.
Graham's great achievement is to make the words jump up from the page, just as Osipova as Lopokova dances through the action, bringing colour and life to a monochrome world.

Few theatre productions can boast the pedigree of THE STANDARD OF LIVING which opened last evening at Theatre Royal Haymarket. Based on the life of economist John Maynard Keynes and written by James Graham (whose recent successes have included Punch and Dear England) the play is far from being a dull academic exercise.
Strange as it sounds, it works perfectly.

cn.t: Graham's ambitious play about economist John Maynard Keynes wins praise for making economics theatrical and thought-provoking, elevated by Kinnear's charming performance and Hytner's polished direction, though some find it overly didactic.
